newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sees higher 1997 grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sees higher 1997 grain harvest.

text.p: Ukraine forecast its 1997 total grain output at 39.1 millon tonnes, up sharply from 25.4 million tonnes last year, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Wednesday.

"Our preliminary plans call for a total grain harvest of 39.1 million tonnes and a winter wheat harvest of 20.8 million tonnes," Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the ministry's crop department, told Reuters.
Ukraine harvested 13.4 million tonnes of winter wheat in 1996.
The ministry forecast total sowing for all spring crops at 15.18 million hectares against 14.55 million hectares last year.
"The spring sowing campaign is going well now and the soil in most parts of the country has enough moisture for a good harvest," he added.

Last month Tymoshenko had forecast a total grain harvest of 38 million tonnes, but Western agricultural experts said the figure was too ambitious in the light of chronic shortages of fertiliser, herbicide, fuel and machinery.
Ukraine had sown 6.63 million hectares with winter wheat this season, about 700,000 with winter rye, and 200,000 hectares with winter barley.
Farmers harvested 16.4 million tonnes of winter wheat in 1995.
